title: Backend (live-animals): fulfilment-copy idempotency recovery runs inside an aborted Mongo transaction — concurrent replay can error instead of returning the existing copy
recipe: No recipe. The fix shape is whatever pp-054 landed for the plant-products equivalent — read that first and transpose it back, so the two implementations converge again rather than diverging further.

filesToTouch.what: The live-animals fulfilment-copy idempotency path. Same defect pp-054's review found in the transposed plant-products copy: the duplicate-key recovery lookup runs inside the same @Transactional method whose insert has just thrown DuplicateKeyException. MongoTransactionManager is registered unconditionally (animals/configuration/MongoConfig.java:91), so this IS a real Mongo transaction and the server-side duplicate-key error can end it — meaning the concurrent loser's recovery read executes through an aborted session and fails, instead of returning the existing copy with 201. Apply the same restructure pp-054 used: keep the single-document insert and its recovery out of the aborted transaction, or recover in a fresh transaction after rollback.

Add a genuinely concurrent integration test over the real HTTP stack: two simultaneous fulfilment-copy requests with the same Idempotency-Key against the same source, both returning 201 with identical body and Location, and exactly one document persisted. Use a CountDownLatch or equivalent so the requests actually overlap. The existing coverage does NOT reach this path — the replay test is sequential and the unit test mocks a successful post-exception lookup, which proves the catch block compiles rather than that the contract holds.

specs: IT: two concurrent fulfilment-copy requests sharing an Idempotency-Key both return 201 with the same body and Location, and exactly one document exists afterwards.
The existing sequential replay behaviour, the unique partial index behaviour, and missing/blank header rejection are all unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: The duplicate-key recovery lookup can no longer execute inside a transaction aborted by the failed insert.

A genuinely concurrent IT proves the losing request returns the existing copy with 201 rather than an error, with exactly one document persisted. A Mockito-fabricated post-exception lookup does not satisfy this criterion.
The live-animals and plant-products idempotency implementations are behaviourally aligned again, restoring Sam's R4 ruling that the two match.
No behaviour change to the sequential replay path, the partial unique index, or header validation.
mvn verify is green end to end, including every pre-existing animals test.
notes:
RAISED DURING THE BUILD (orchestrator, 2026-08-01), not by the planners, and it is a defect in ALREADY-SHIPPED live-animals code rather than in anything this programme wrote. Found by transposition: pp-054 copied the animals idempotency scheme per Sam's ruling R4 ('match live-animals exactly'), and reviewing the copy surfaced a flaw that had gone unnoticed in the original. The orchestrator independently verified the premise before acting — MongoTransactionManager is a plain unconditional @Bean at animals/configuration/MongoConfig.java:91 and the copy method is @Transactional, so there genuinely is a transaction to abort.

WHY IT CARRIES A GATE: this edits shipped live-animals production code on a path that is exercised in a real deployment, and the failure it fixes is a race that current tests do not reach. That combination — shipped code, concurrency, no existing coverage of the path — is worth a human look before it lands, which is why the increment halts for review rather than landing autonomously.

WHY pp-054 DID NOT JUST FIX BOTH: pp-054's scope is the plant-products package. Reaching into animals from a plant-products increment would have put a concurrency change to shipped code inside a diff nobody was reviewing for that, and R4 alignment is restored by this increment instead. The R4 deviation is deliberate and is recorded in WHEN-YOURE-BACK.md: R4 means 'do not invent a different scheme', not 'faithfully reproduce a concurrency bug'.

SCOPE FENCE: the idempotency recovery path and its test coverage. Do not refactor the surrounding fulfilment service, and do not change the sequential replay semantics.
openQuestions: Is the same aborted-transaction recovery pattern used anywhere else in the animals package — any other @Transactional method that catches DuplicateKeyException and then reads? If so this is a class of bug rather than one instance, and the fix should sweep them together.
Does this need a Jira ticket in its own right, given it is a defect in shipped code rather than programme work? The orchestrator's view is yes, but that is Sam's call and no ticket has been raised.
